item.name: Planner self-healing verdict loop
item.contract: Architecture planner consumes autoloop health/ledger outcomes, stamps planner-owned verdicts, retries validation-safe regenerations, and escalates rows that stay failing after repeated reshapes
item.degraded_mode: Rows that resist planner reshapes are marked needs_human and removed from default autoloop selection instead of silently cycling.
ready_when: Autoloop row health blocks and planner trigger events exist on main.
not_ready_when: The slice relies on live LLM calls or manual ledger edits instead of deterministic planner/autoloop fixtures.
acceptance: PlannerVerdict round-trips and is preserved by autoloop health writes.
Planner self-evaluation distinguishes unstuck, still_failing, and no_attempts_yet outcomes.
NeedsHuman is sticky after the configured reshape threshold, and autoloop skips those rows by default.
item.note: Complete: architectureplanner now records planner ledger events, consumes trigger/cursor state, evaluates previous reshapes against autoloop outcomes, retries validation failures with feedback, stamps PlannerVerdict reshape counts/outcomes, escalates persistent failures to needs_human, and exposes needs-human rows in status while autoloop skips them by default.
done_signal: Planner lifecycle tests prove trigger consumption, reshape self-evaluation, PlannerVerdict stamping, sticky needs_human escalation, and autoloop candidate skipping.

provenance.note: PlannerVerdict, planner retry/self-evaluation, and needs_human selection are Gormes-owned autoloop control-plane behavior.

item.name: External review feedback ingestion for planner rows
item.contract: gormes-planner and gormes-review-loop define a bounded, source-backed workflow for ingesting external review feedback such as Greptile/Grep-style PR reviews, GitHub review comments, CI annotations, and static-analysis findings into existing progress rows or one new builder-ready row without creating a side backlog.
item.degraded_mode: If exact review evidence is unavailable, agents must stop and ask for reviewer text, PR/check URLs, file paths, command output, or copied review logs before shaping rows.
ready_when: The external review evidence is available as exact text, PR comment URLs, CI annotations, local review logs, or copied reviewer output.
The pass can classify each finding as an existing-row refinement, a new builder-ready row, a duplicate, or out-of-scope noise.
No runtime code change is required in the planner pass.
not_ready_when: The review feedback is summarized without exact reviewer text, file path, command output, or PR/check evidence.
The pass would auto-apply broad code changes instead of planning one bounded row or row refinement.
The proposed output is a TODO file, issue list, or private queue outside progress.json.
acceptance: gormes-planner names external review ingestion as a planner-owned route and says findings must become progress row refinements or one builder-ready row.
gormes-review-loop tells agents to capture exact review evidence first, then route row-shaping work through gormes-planner when the fix is not already builder-ready.
Skill routing docs include Greptile/Grep-style PR review feedback as a review-loop to planner chain.
The workflow preserves progress.json as the only backlog and rejects review side queues.
done_signal: Planner and review-loop skills now route exact external review findings into canonical progress-row updates, and progress/docs validation passes without adding a side backlog.

provenance.note: Gormes-owned control-plane workflow inspired by Juan's request to add gormes-planner plus Greptile/Grep-style review feedback into planning.

item.name: Gormes update release planner and dry-run contract
item.contract: `gormes update` must distinguish normal release-installed operators from managed source checkouts before it mutates anything. For release installs, the command plans against trusted GitHub Releases: detect install layout, current version/build, OS/arch artifact name, channel policy (`stable` by default, `development` explicit), latest release metadata, snapshot path, components to update, blocked reasons, and whether an update is available. `gormes update --dry-run` prints the exact non-mutating plan; `gormes update --check` performs no mutation and exits 0 when current, 10 when an update is available, and nonzero for check errors. Existing source-checkout behavior from `Self-update command lifecycle safety` remains the managed/dev path and must not be silently used for release installs.
item.degraded_mode: Unknown install layout, unsupported OS/arch, missing release metadata, channel mismatch, dirty unmanaged source checkout, and network/API lookup failures produce typed plan blockers without changing binaries, assets, skills, services, config, credentials, sessions, memory, or source checkouts.
source_refs: cmd/gormes/update.go:newUpdateCommandWithSeams (current source-checkout update command and injectable seams)
install.sh:decide_install_method + fetch_release_binary (release asset naming, GitHub latest release lookup, SHA-256 sidecar evidence)
scripts/install.ps1:release binary fetch block (Windows release asset naming and SHA-256 sidecar evidence)
Completed row: Self-update command lifecycle safety (source-checkout update path remains intact)
ready_when: The existing source-checkout `gormes update` command and lifecycle seams are complete and validated.
Installer release-binary fetch behavior already defines trusted repo, platform artifact names, release channels, and SHA-256 sidecar expectations.
Tests can inject install layout, current build, release metadata, OS/arch, channel, and clock without network or filesystem mutation.
not_ready_when: The slice downloads or swaps binaries, syncs skills/assets, restarts services, or pulls git remotes.
Release-installed binaries silently fall back to managed source checkout mutation.
`--check` or `--dry-run` writes update logs, snapshots, config, skills, sessions, services, or source checkout state.
Exit codes for current/update-available/error are not deterministic and tested.
unblocks: Gormes update verified binary swap and rollback
acceptance: Release install, managed source checkout, unmanaged source checkout, and unknown install layouts are classified with typed evidence.

`gormes update --dry-run` prints current version/build, target version/build, source (`github_release` or `managed_source`), channel, artifact, snapshot path, component plan, and blockers without mutation.
`gormes update --check` exits 0 when current, 10 when an update is available, and nonzero for check errors, with JSON and text reports carrying the same state.

Stable vs development channel policy is explicit; release installs use GitHub Releases by default, managed source/dev installs use the existing source lifecycle only when detected or explicitly requested.
No binary, asset, skill, service, config, credential, session, memory, git checkout, or update ledger file changes during planner/check/dry-run tests.
item.note: Builder-ready row 1 of the grilled release-update cluster. It deliberately avoids mutation so the release-installed operator contract can be proven before binary replacement, bundled asset/skill sync, or service coordination.
done_signal: Update planner fixtures prove release/source/unknown layout detection, current-vs-target metadata, stable/development channel policy, dry-run output, --check exit codes, and zero mutation before any release artifact install path exists.

provenance.note: grill_origin: 2026-05-16 operator plan for a safer `gormes update` command. This row extends the completed Hermes-style managed source updater with Gormes-owned release-install planning semantics for the single-binary distribution.

evidence: RED: go test ./cmd/gormes ./internal/cli -run 'TestUpdateReleasePlanner|TestUpdateCommandReleaseDryRun|TestUpdateCommandCheck' -count=1 failed because BuildUpdateReleasePlan, release update metadata types, install-kind/channel/source enums, and update command release-planner seams did not exist.

GREEN: internal/cli/update_release_plan.go adds the pure release update planner with typed install layout classification, github_release vs managed_source routing, stable/development channel blockers, platform artifact naming, snapshot/component plans, current-vs-target version/build comparison, and typed degraded blockers.

GREEN: cmd/gormes/update.go adds --dry-run and --channel, routes release-installed --check and all --dry-run invocations through the non-mutating planner, emits JSON/text plan reports with build provenance, returns exit 0/current, 10/update-available, and 1/blocker, and keeps existing source-checkout lifecycle behavior for managed-source checks.
